FACT_ID: sec04-R01 | anchor: A01
The two approved hand positions are 3 and 9 o'clock or 4 and 8 o'clock; the classic ten-and-two answer is not what this handbook gives. [A01]
Why it matters: group vehicle control; difficulty two; prereq sec04-F22. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-R02 | anchor: A01
Mirror setup differs by side: for the left mirror your head touches the left window, for the right mirror your head is centered under the inside mirror. [A01]
Why it matters: group vehicle setup; difficulty two; confusable sec04-F14 vs sec04-F15. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-R03 | anchor: A01
Steering in reverse follows the same rule as forward driving: turn the wheel toward where you want the vehicle to go. [A01]
Why it matters: group vehicle control; difficulty two; prereq sec04-F21. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-R04 | anchor: A01
A bouncing car points to two possible checks: tires when it bounces with a shaking wheel or pull, suspension when it keeps bouncing after a bump or stop. [A01]
Why it matters: group vehicle maintenance; difficulty two; confusable sec04-F10 vs sec04-F11. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec04-R05 | anchor: A01
When pressing the accelerator, the ball of the foot works the pedal while the heel stays on the floor; when starting the engine, the right foot is on the brake. [A01]
Why it matters: group basic driving; difficulty one; confusable sec04-F18 vs sec04-F19. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0009]

Misconception: a quick glance at your phone is not a distraction; any momentary loss of attention counts. [A01]
Misconception: the head restraint is a neck pillow set low; it should touch the back of your head. [A01]
Misconception: an idling car is safe in a closed garage for a short time; exhaust can kill very quickly. [A01]
Mnemonic: Fingers, not palms; thumbs up, never inside the rim. [A01]
Glossary: Rubbernecking means staring at something of interest while driving. [A01]
Glossary: Hydroplaning means tires riding on a film of water and losing grip, made likelier by worn tires. [A01]
Glossary: Road rage means letting anger control your driving toward others. [A01]
